title: Define autograder runner contract + build the sandboxed CI correctness backend (no network, FS read-only, CPU/mem/time caps, non-root)
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). The correctness gate is the single most important quality mechanism in the curriculum: every exercise's reference solution must be proven to pass its test suite in CI before it can publish, and the starter code must fail those same tests. Without a working, sandboxed runner contract this gate cannot exist and the correctness guarantee collapses.
objective: Define the language-agnostic runner contract (run(code, tests, limits) → { passed, failures[], stdout, durationMs, resourceUse }) and implement the sandboxed CI correctness backend with a Python adapter, so that CI can set solutionVerified:true when the reference solution passes and fail the build when it does not.
acceptanceCriteria: Runner contract is defined: run(code, tests, limits) → { passed: boolean, failures: string[], stdout: string, durationMs: number, resourceUse: object }; contract is language-agnostic and documented.
A Python adapter implements the contract and executes code + tests in the CI sandbox.

CI sandbox enforces: no network access, read-only filesystem, CPU and memory caps, wall-clock time limit, and non-root execution; a solution that hangs, exceeds limits, or touches the network fails the gate.
CI sets solutionVerified:true only when the reference solution passes its tests.
CI asserts starter code does NOT already pass the tests (starter-must-fail check).
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass.
A solution that attempts network access, exceeds resource limits, or hangs is demonstrated to fail the gate in a test case.
output: A merged PR adding the runner contract definition, the Python adapter, and the sandboxed CI correctness backend, with documentation of the contract interface and sandbox constraints.
